A while loop, because the iteration count is unknown

A while loop, because the iteration count is known

draftItems.prompt: A classroom app displays a 6 by 6 grid of student names. The app uses a nested loop to visit every cell. How many inner operations does the pair of loops perform?
draftItems.reformulatedPrompt: A classroom app displays a 6 by 6 grid of student names. The app uses a nested loop to visit every cell. How many inner operations does the pair of loops perform?
scenarioAssumptions: A classroom app displays a 6 by 6 grid of student names.
draftItems.explanation: With nested loops, if both loops traverse n elements, the pair can perform n squared inner operations. Here n is 6, so the inner operations are 6 squared, which is 36.
options: 36 inner operations
12 inner operations
6 inner operations
6 squared inner operations

draftItems.reformulatedPrompt: Explain how nested loops behave: for each selected outer-loop iteration, what happens with the inner loop?

requiredIdeas: Nested loops run an inner loop for each selected outer-loop iteration.

draftItems.prompt: Analyze Accumulator initialization through two evidence-supported cases: Case A — sum accumulator; Case B — identity value. Which option correctly accounts for both cases using the relevant evidence?
draftItems.reformulatedPrompt: Analyze Accumulator initialization through two evidence-supported cases: Case A — sum accumulator; Case B — identity value. Which option correctly accounts for both cases using the relevant evidence?
draftItems.explanation: An accumulator stores a running result such as a sum, and it must be initialized to the identity value appropriate to the operation, such as zero for addition.
options: An accumulator stores a running result and must be initialized to the identity value, such as zero for addition.
An accumulator stores a running result but must be initialized to one for addition.
An accumulator stores a final result and must be initialized to the operation's result.
An accumulator stores a running result and must be initialized to the first input value.

draftItems.prompt: A classroom app reads student ID numbers until the value 0 appears, and 0 is not a real student ID. Which loop behavior correctly applies the sentinel rule for this loop?
draftItems.reformulatedPrompt: A classroom app reads student ID numbers until the value 0 appears, and 0 is not a real student ID. Which loop behavior correctly applies the sentinel rule for this loop?
scenarioAssumptions: A classroom app reads student ID numbers until the value 0 appears, and 0 is not a real student ID.
draftItems.explanation: A sentinel-controlled loop stops after reading a distinguished input value, so the loop stops when the sentinel 0 is read.
options: The loop stops after reading the sentinel input value 0.
The loop continues after reading the sentinel input value 0.
The loop stops before reading any input value.
The loop stops only after reading a non-sentinel input value.

draftItems.prompt: A library checkout program reads book barcode numbers until the value -1 appears, and -1 is not a real barcode. When should the program test the sentinel before including it in a calculation?
draftItems.reformulatedPrompt: A library checkout program reads book barcode numbers until the value -1 appears, and -1 is not a real barcode. When should the program test the sentinel before including it in a calculation?
scenarioAssumptions: A library checkout program reads book barcode numbers until the value -1 appears, and -1 is not a real barcode.
draftItems.explanation: The sentinel should be tested before it is included in a calculation when it is not real data, so the program must check for -1 before using it in any calculation.
options: Test the sentinel before including it in the calculation.
Include the sentinel in the calculation before testing it.
Test the sentinel only after the calculation is complete.
Never test the sentinel because it is not real data.

draftItems.prompt: Analyze Loop invariants through two evidence-supported cases: Case A — Loop invariants; Case B — the loop produces the intended result explanation. Which option correctly analyzes both cases using the two evidence facts?
draftItems.reformulatedPrompt: Analyze Loop invariants through two evidence-supported cases: Case A — Loop invariants; Case B — the loop produces the intended result explanation. Which option correctly analyzes both cases using the two evidence facts?
draftItems.explanation: Loop invariants describe facts that remain true before and after every iteration, and they help explain why the loop produces the intended result when it terminates.
options: Loop invariants remain true before and after every iteration, and they help explain why the loop produces the intended result when it terminates.
Loop invariants change after each iteration, and they help explain why the loop produces an unintended result when it terminates.
Loop invariants describe facts that remain true only before the first iteration, and they help explain why the loop produces the intended result when it starts.
Loop invariants describe facts that remain true after every iteration, but they do not help explain why the loop produces the intended result when it terminates.
